exposure: GTT results: normal, single pathological value, or gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM)
Third trimester oral glucose tolerance test (GTT) results
third trimester oral glucose tolerance test (GTT) following normal glucose challenge test (GCT)
outcome: Perinatal outcomes (birth weight, cesarean delivery rate, neonatal outcomes)
cohort: 323 women with a normal 50 g glucose challenge test (<140 mg/dl) followed by GTT, who delivered a live-born fetus >28 gestational weeks
finding: Treatment of late-onset GDM may lead to lower birthweights, presumably due to glucose control.
mod_finding: While there was no statistically significant association between late-onset GDM and cesarean delivery after adjusting for confounders, the study does not mention mode of delivery as a factor influencing GDM diagnosis.
birth_weight: Infants of mothers diagnosed and treated as GDM had lower birth weights compared to non-diabetics and those with a single pathological value GTT.
